Name: Bradley Tusk
Details: Mobile Voting Project (founded by Bradley Tusk) funds VoteSecure, an open-source cryptographic SDK for end-to-end verifiable mobile voting released Nov 2025. It is not a complete voting system; election vendors must integrate it. Active on legislation in CO, MD, MN, NJ, and VT. Seeking election officials and legislators. Its security claims are disputed by election security researchers.

Name: Civic Match
Problem Topic: Talent Pipeline; Hiring Process; Workforce Development
Details: Civic Match is a free platform connecting public servants with state and local government roles; 12,000+ job seekers and 258 governments had used it by Feb 2026. Talent Accelerator runs free 8-week workshops for city HR teams (spring 2026 cohort included NYC; fall 2026 cohort on data-driven hiring). The Responsive Cities Network fellowship closed in Jan 2026.

Name: FAS Impact Fellowship
Details: Places scientists and technologists in short tours of service in federal and state government using existing hiring authorities. No open fellow positions listed as of Sept 2026. Agencies can request support and submit openings for fully or partially funded placements.

Name: AI Government Leadership Program
Problem Topic: AI in Government; Hiring Architecture; Talent Pipeline; Iterative Learning; Workforce Development
Details: Free 6-session program training senior government leaders (GS-15, SES, state and local executives) on AI strategy. No technical background required. Fall 2026 federal and state/local applications are closed. Supported by Microsoft and Google.org. Next cycle not yet posted.

Name: Code for America AI Government Partnership
Details: Partners with state and local agencies on AI for benefits delivery. Its SNAP Policy Navigator, built with Anthropic, was announced in May 2026 as a caseworker pilot. Also publishes the 2026 Government AI Landscape Assessment on state AI readiness. Reach out to explore a partnership.

Name: Free AI Training for Government
Details: Free live workshops and self-paced courses for public servants on responsible AI and innovation. Fall 2026 series include Benchmarking AI, AI and Energy, Procurement, and Public Health. Agencies can access or partner at no cost.

Name: State Capacity USCIS Project
Offering: Collaboration Opportunity; Expertise; Interesting Conversation; Problem to Solve; Tool / Product
Problem Area: Procurement & Operations; Service Delivery; Talent & Hiring; Technology & Data
Problem Topic: Benefits Access; Data Integration; Data Security; Hiring Architecture; Hiring Process; Legacy Systems; Operational Excellence; Procurement Reform; Reaction Time; Regulatory & Administrative Burden; Service Design; Shared Platforms; Talent Pipeline; Workforce Development
Details: Led by former USCIS Director Ur Jaddou and Emilie Hyams. Designs cross-partisan administrative reforms for timely, fair immigration service delivery at USCIS. Per the submission, seeking roughly $2M per year through 2030 (mainly expert salaries) plus expert collaborators.

Name: Voting Information Project (VIP)
Details: Free program, run by Democracy Works since 2018, that partners with state and local election offices to publish official polling place and ballot data to major platforms. Offices review and approve data before publication. Participation is voluntary.

Name: American Connection Corps
Details: AmeriCorps service fellowship placing members with local governments and nonprofits on digital access and economic opportunity. Recruiting members for the Sept 2026 to Aug 2027 term. Governments and nonprofits can host; standard host cost is $35K per member per year.

Name: Cornell Tech Urban Innovation Fellowship
Organization: Urban Tech Hub at Cornell Tech
Details: Two-year fellowship embedding mid-career technologists in NYC agencies on high-priority projects. Launched Nov 2024 with seven fellows, with Bloomberg Philanthropies support. No open application as of Sept 2026.

Name: Government Innovation Fellowship
Details: Paid embedded fellowship (~$92K) placing graduate-level professionals with state and local governments on performance improvement in housing, child welfare, and safety and justice. The Sept 3, 2026 deadline has passed. Main application window typically opens late winter or early spring.

Name: TechCongress
Details: Places technologists as tech policy advisors in congressional offices, including committee and leadership staff. January 2027 cohort applications are closed (deadline was late June 2026). Next cohort (January 2028) applications open summer 2027.

Name: AI Readiness Project
Details: With Rockefeller Foundation funding, supports states, territories, and Tribal Nations with AI pilots, cross-state working groups, and shared tools such as evaluation frameworks and procurement templates. AI Knowledge Hub launched July 2026. Status of 2026 pilot recruitment unconfirmed.

Name: Barr Fellowship
Details: 15-month fellowship for Massachusetts-focused social change leaders, centered on rest, learning, and organizational wellbeing. Class of 2026 applications closed June 30, 2026; finalists notified by Nov 5, 2026.

Name: Bloomberg Harvard City Hall Fellows
Details: Fully funded two-year fellowship placing recent Harvard master's and professional degree graduates in city halls on mayoral priorities. 2026 deadline has passed; applications open each spring semester.

Name: Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative
Details: Nine-month management program for mayors plus two senior officials per city. Tenth class of 46 mayors began July 2026. Participation is by selection, not open application. Participating cities become eligible for a City Hall Fellow.

Name: Bobby Zipp
Offering: Expertise; Interesting Conversation; Problem to Solve
Problem Area: Domains; Procurement & Operations; Service Delivery; Technology & Data
Problem Topic: AI in Government; Criminal Justice; Legacy Systems; Procurement Reform; Regulatory & Administrative Burden; Service Design
Details: I work for a prosecutor's office as the Chief Data Officer - I oversee all data analytics initiatives across the office, and improving our data analytics capabilities often requires modernizing our operations in partnership with other parts of my office.

Name: Ideas for Impact RFEI
Organization: New York City Economic Development Corporation
Details: Open call for partnership ideas that fall outside NYCEDC's other solicitations: programs, technology pilots, capital projects, impact investments. NYCEDC mainly offers in-kind support (assets, marketing, technical assistance). Reviewed monthly; final deadline Dec 31, 2026, 4 PM.

Name: Presidential Innovation Fellows
Details: Federal fellowship (since 2012) embedding senior technologists at partner agencies for a yearlong tour. The 2026 class of 17 fellows launched April 2026 across 10 agencies. Applications closed; recruits annually.

Name: TechAccess: AI-Ready America
Details: $224M program for up to 56 State/Territory AI Coordination Hubs, up to $1M per year for 3 years. Round 2 (20 hubs): LOI due Dec 15, 2026, full proposal Jan 15, 2027. One proposal per institution. Note: the solicitation prints the Round 2 LOI year as 2027, an apparent typo.

Name: US Tech Force
Details: Federal hiring initiative for about 1,000 technologists in 1-2 year roles, $150-200K. Focus on AI, cybersecurity, data, and software. About 200 hired as of late May 2026, with a stated target of 300 to 500 by end of summer. Applications via techforce.gov.

Name: CITP Technology Fellows
Organization: Center for Information Technology Policy (CITP, Princeton)
Details: Non-resident fellowship for technologists with government experience who advise state and local regulators on AI, privacy, and cybersecurity. Inaugural cohort announced 2026. Next application cycle not yet posted.

Name: Election Cybersecurity Initiative
Details: Nonpartisan initiative supporting election administrators on cybersecurity through research, analysis, and convenings, filling gaps left by reduced federal election security support.

Name: Georgetown Beeck Center Innovation Fellowship
Details: Innovation and Incubation Fellowship (12-24 months) for senior practitioners piloting new civic tech projects. Fellows are hired role by role through Georgetown job postings (e.g., AI Fellow), not a standing open call. Check the Beeck Center careers page.

Name: Stanford RegLab Government Partnership
Problem Topic: Evidence Use; Data Integration; AI in Government
Details: Partners with agencies at every level on AI, machine learning, and causal inference. Past partners include IRS, EPA, DOL, Santa Clara County, San Diego, and the San Francisco City Attorney. Reach out to explore a partnership.

Name: State & Local Innovation Evaluation Incubator
Details: Evaluation Incubator: state and local governments apply for technical assistance, flexible funding, and researcher matchmaking to design randomized evaluations. Partner RFP listed as open; researcher RFP closed. 18 government partners since 2015.

Name: CiviForm Government Deployment
Details: Free open-source no-code application hub for public benefits, stewarded by Exygy with Google.org support. Governments host and control their data. Used by Seattle, Bloomington IN, Charlotte NC, and Arkansas. Named a TIME Best Invention of 2025.

Name: Dev Doshi
Offering: Collaboration Opportunity; Expertise; Interesting Conversation; Tool / Product
Problem Area: Open to Any; Domains; Participatory Democracy; Talent & Hiring; Technology & Data; Test & Learn
Problem Topic: AI in Government; Broadband & Internet Connectivity; Child Welfare; Civic Engagement; Criminal Justice; Data Integration; Data Security; Democracy Infrastructure; Economic Mobility; Education Delivery; Evidence Use; Expert Contribution; Feedback Loops; Hiring Architecture; Hiring Process; Housing & Land Use; Iterative Learning; Legacy Systems; Outcomes Measurement; Permitting & Licensing; Physical Infrastructure; Scaling What Works; Shared Platforms; Talent Pipeline; Tax & Revenue; Transparency & Accountability; Workforce Development

Name: Jeremie Ponak
Details: Building open AI benchmarks for government - evaluating model accuracy on benefits eligibility, service delivery, and healthcare policy. Starting with SNAP. Seeking researchers and civic technologists working on AI evaluation for public sector.

Name: Mirilla Zhu
Organization: Legislative Information Access in Prisons and Jails
Problem Topic: Broadband & Internet Connectivity; Civic Engagement; Criminal Justice; Democracy Infrastructure; Shared Platforms
Details: I'm building a version of Open States to make legislative information accessible in prisons and jails in real-time. Would love to connect with beta testers and people in government/DOC who might have interest and authority to make this resource available in facilities!

Name: Pro-Bono Tech Volunteer Network
Details: Free, nonpartisan network that matches pro-bono technologists with governments and nonprofits. Governments request help directly through the site. Focus areas include AI, benefits, and service delivery.

Name: Tal Roded
Offering: Collaboration Opportunity; Expertise; Interesting Conversation; Tool / Product
Problem Area: Service Delivery; Technology & Data; Test & Learn
Problem Topic: Service Design; Shared Platforms; Evidence Use
Details: Data scientist building open civic tech tools for NYC government: State Capacity Ecosystem Hub, NYC Government Bodies Explorer, Fiscal Impact Statement tracker. Seeking collaborators on government data infrastructure, urban policy, and civic tech.

Name: Toxin Scout Environmental Health Records Lookup
Details: Free public tool that makes EPA and government environmental health records easier to search by city, helping residents, journalists, planners, and civic technologists find source-linked data.

Name: Alex Johnston
Details: good sense is an AI driven diagnostic platform that allows cities and states to self-diagnose their service delivery challenges. See how your service works end to end, trace each problem to its root cause, and know which fix will actually move the needle.

Name: Jeremy Ney
Offering: Expertise; Interesting Conversation; Job / Fellowship; Problem to Solve; Tool / Product

Name: NYC Urban Fellows Program
Organization: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS)
Details: Nine-month paid fellowship placing recent graduates in mayoral offices and City agencies, with a leadership seminar series. Application closed; DCAS says the next application opens Fall 2026. Penn lists a tentative Jan 12, 2027 deadline (unconfirmed by DCAS).

Name: Coding it Forward
Details: Paid 10-week summer fellowship for early-career technologists in federal, state, and local government (now one Coding it Forward Fellowship, formerly Civic Digital Fellowship and Civic Innovation Corps). Last cycle opened Oct 15; 2027 window not yet posted.

Name: Tech Talent Project
Problem Area: Talent & Hiring; Procurement & Operations; Service Delivery
Problem Topic: Talent Pipeline; Hiring Architecture; Service Design
Details: Medicaid Delivery Innovation Initiative: no-cost 7-week discovery sprints and recruitment support for state Medicaid agencies ahead of federal requirements taking effect Jan 1, 2027. Network of 11,000+ technologists. Also state transitions, Tech to Gov, and Tech Executive Leadership Initiative.

Name: Accountability and Reform Research Consortium (ARRC)
Problem Area: Talent & Hiring; Procurement & Operations; Technology & Data
Problem Topic: Workforce Development; Hiring Architecture; Operational Excellence; Data Integration
Details: Cross-university consortium convened by the Volcker Alliance documenting the impact of federal workforce and program cuts on service delivery and governance. Awarded 6 stipends (Mar 2026) and 11 stipends (Jun 2026) via RFPs. No open RFP as of Sept 2026; institutions and scholars can join.

Name: Research Report Stipends
Organization: IBM Center for The Business of Government
Problem Area: Procurement & Operations; Technology & Data; Talent & Hiring
Problem Topic: Operational Excellence; Data Integration; Procurement Reform; Workforce Development
Details: $20,000 stipends for academics, nonprofit researchers, and journalists (not government employees) to write practical 10,000-12,000 word reports. Fall 2026 call due Nov 2, 2026 across five areas: multi-sector partnerships, financial and operational effectiveness, technology, data, and the government workforce.

Name: Jess Lowry
Problem Area: Participatory Democracy; Service Delivery; Technology & Data
Problem Topic: Civic Engagement; Democracy Infrastructure; Legacy Systems; Service Design; Shared Platforms; Transparency & Accountability
Details: I have 20 years of experience designing and facilitating multi-day, in-person sessions that help teams navigate change, solve complex problems, and develop practical plans for moving forward. I use a sociotechnical approach to help teams co-design operational change.

Name: Karan
Offering: Collaboration Opportunity; Interesting Conversation; Tool / Product
Details: We're building the largest online global community of public servants who want to learn from each others' successes and failures, and ultimately deliver better work. So we want to understand how to facilitate online learning from peers to create maximum value for public servants.

Name: Patrick Atwater
Details: I run the innovation program at SoCal's Metropolitan Water District, where I'm building out a pilot fund and trying to get good ideas to actually ship inside a legacy public agency. I also spend time with the Protocol Institute thinking about coordination and institutional design

Name: Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program
Organization: Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University
Details: Inaugural residency (one semester or full year) for researchers studying urban problem-solving and city leadership. Housing and financial support provided. Requires a PhD and a current faculty or research appointment. Apply by Oct 28, 2026; selections in Feb 2027.

Name: AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellowships
Organization: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
Details: Places scientists and engineers in federal policy roles; running since 1973. Applications for the 2027-2028 class close Nov 1, 2026.

Name: Community-Centered PITathon RFP (Y5 2026-2027)
Details: Funds hackathons (PITathons) hosted by PIT-UN member institutions in New England, New York, the Midwest, and the West. Prioritizes genuinely new, community-authored models; not accepting iterations of past models. Deadline not shown on the public page; confirm with PIT-UN.

Name: GovAI Coalition
Details: Free coalition of 900+ government agencies sharing responsible AI policies, templates, and contracts. Government members can chair committees; academia and nonprofits can co-chair. Annual summit Dec 9-11, 2026 in San Jose.

Name: What Works Cities Certification
Details: Free benchmark of city data practices against a 43-criteria standard, with a roadmap and peer network. Open to cities of 30,000+ in the Americas. Start with the Data Snapshot.

Name: Govern For America Fellowship (2027)
Details: Two-year paid fellowship placing early-career leaders in state and local government roles. 2027 application opens Dec 14, 2026, reviewed on a rolling basis. Governments can also apply to host a fellow.

Name: Code for America Summit 2027: Call for Proposals and Demo Lab
Details: Summit 2027 is in Washington, DC. Calls for session proposals and Demo Lab submissions have not been announced; last year the call ran Nov 13-24, so expect mid-November (inferred from pattern).

Name: NYC Open Data Week 2027: Event Organizers
Organization: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation / BetaNYC / Data Through Design
Details: Annual March festival of community-run events on NYC public data. Anyone can host an event. Next festival March 2027; the call for event proposals has not been posted yet.

Name: Early Career Talent Network
Details: Centralized pool where early-career candidates express interest in roles across multiple federal agencies. Starts with finance, HR, engineering, project management, and procurement. Replaces the earlier Data Science and Project Management Fellows listings.
